questions.q: How does Project 3's risk profile differ from Projects 1 and 2?
options: It doesn't use an LLM at all
Projects 1 and 2 answer questions; Project 3 takes real actions, some of which can't be cleanly undone once executed
Project 3 has no risk at all, unlike the first two projects
There is no meaningful difference between the three projects
questions.explain: A RAG assistant and a read-only data analyst only answer questions. A tool-using agent with write-capable tools can take irreversible actions, which is exactly why this project builds in a human approval checkpoint.

questions.q: What are the two things this lesson says make a good fit when scoping your own Project 3 tool set?
options: The cheapest possible API and the simplest possible UI
At least one tool with a real, hard-to-reverse consequence, and a plausible real reason a human needs to be in the loop
Exactly ten tools and no system prompt
A tool that requires no JSON schema at all
questions.explain: A consequential, hard-to-reverse tool plus a genuine reason for human oversight (cost, risk, irreversibility, compliance) is what makes the approval workflow in Lesson 15 meaningful rather than decorative.

questions.q: Which lesson in Chapter 4 specifically builds the approve/reject checkpoint?
options: Lesson 13
Lesson 14
Lesson 15
Lesson 17
questions.explain: Lesson 15, 'Building the Approval Workflow,' is where the actual human-in-the-loop checkpoint gets built.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about tools that only look information up, with no side effects?
options: They are the only kind of tool allowed in Project 3
They typically don't need the human approval checkpoint -- it's reserved for tools with real consequences
They must always be approved before running, same as any other tool
They cannot be included in the tool set at all
questions.explain: A good project shape includes one or two low-risk, read-only tools alongside at least one higher-risk tool that always stops for sign-off -- approval is reserved for the consequential action.

questions.q: Which existing course does this lesson say Project 3 directly applies, not merely reviews?
options: The Power BI course
The AI Agents course -- its tool schemas, human-in-the-loop patterns, and guardrails
The Tableau course
The Terraform & Bicep course
questions.explain: This project is built directly on the AI Agents course's tool-design and human-in-the-loop material, used here as the actual foundation rather than a recap.
